indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the two currency abbreviations

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for a euro, so two euros give two Es

indicators.note: possible suggests one of several possible arrangements of the word saving

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up whether a saving could be made in euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Euros' looks like the currency being saved in, but each euro is just its abbreviation E; 'possible' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to picture or contemplate it, a synonym of consider.

clue.text: Composer gets street atlas to look up city

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the joined pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
an A-Z is the standard British street atlas of a city

explanation.surface: A composer consults a street atlas to find a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to look up' turns BERGAZ round as a whole; the A-Z is a British book of street maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: H is for a lot of liquor

parts.note: the letter H is the first letter, or head, of the word hogs

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry claiming the letter H stands for plenty of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the head of HOGS is H, so 'H' is the HOG'S HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, and a measure of roughly fifty gallons of beer or wine.

definitions.meaning: the first of May, when workers and the labour movement hold marches
the international radio call that signals a ship or aircraft in danger

explanation.surface: A workers' march day is also the cry for help.
explanation.definitionFit: May Day is the traditional labour festival, and the radio call mayday signals an emergency.

indicators.note: devastated implies the word Cleans is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone clears up a ravaged scene of slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges CLEANS. Senlac Hill is the site of the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Senlac is the ridge where the Battle of Hastings was fought, a site of great slaughter.

definitions.meaning: a bent wire clip that binds papers together

explanation.surface: The chief part of some fastening device.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a wire clip for paper and also a principal commodity or basic item.

parts.note: looks like leftovers from a roast, but read as the ash left by a smoked cannabis joint

explanation.surface: What's left over from the Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot is cannabis, so a smoked joint leaves pot ash.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash, a potassium compound, was originally made from wood ashes, and literally pot ash is cannabis residue.

definitions.meaning: A British aircraft maker, of the Hurricane and Harrier
a street seller who goes about peddling goods

explanation.surface: An aircraft salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawker is a pedlar, and Hawker was a famous British aircraft manufacturer.

clue.text: Amélie has it, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Amélie has it, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Amélie has it, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: the name carries a diacritic over its first e, and a charming French way of talking is also suggested

explanation.surface: The French film heroine has a charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: the mark over the é in Amélie, and a cute way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark on the é in Amélie is the diacritic sloping up to the right.

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge

explanation.surface: A weapon that backs up the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender sword, and also a British surface-to-air missile.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Paddy Ashdown was the leader of the British Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: An Irishman is caught on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' tempts as an Irishman or a temper; it is the politician Paddy Ashdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying at once, which is paying ready money.

indicators.note: read as un-certain: the word for certain is taken away

parts.note: pleasure is gratification

explanation.surface: Unsure whether this justification will satisfy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' is split as un + certain: remove SURE from PLEASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an excuse or appeal offered in defence.

parts.note: a gunlayer aims artillery, but read as a layer kept among a battery, like guns in a row

explanation.surface: A soldier who aims artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: A battery is a group of guns and also a row of cages; a hen in one is a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery hen is a laying hen kept in a cage, a layer from a battery.

clue.text: Cherie's man does start unexpectedly to deliver the goods

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals that these letters fall into a surprising new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of does is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cherie Blair's husband sets out to deliver on his promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes D from 'does'; 'unexpectedly' rearranges CHERIESMAN with that D.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandise is goods for sale, the stock a trader deals in.

clue.text: Lamb on a string is a princess

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another comes below it

parts.note: a cord is a string
Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: A lamb on a lead turns out to be royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts ELIA beneath CORD. Lamb is the essayist Charles Lamb, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is King Lear's youngest daughter in Shakespeare's play.

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
ties are things that fasten

explanation.surface: Checking the straps on some lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanties is an informal word for skimpy knickers.

clue.text: Poor Roy can be remembered as nosy

indicators.note: poor indicates the letters of Roy can are badly formed and must be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Poor Roy may go down in memory as a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges ROYCAN. 'nosy' means big-nosed here, not inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrano de Bergerac is famed in Rostand's play for his enormous nose.

clue.text: College tutor's first with the wine

parts.note: Clare is a Cambridge college

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of tutor's

explanation.surface: A college tutor heads off with the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College' is not just C here but Clare College, Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

indicators.note: going ballistic means flying into a wild rage, so the letters of It's Charley explode into a new order

explanation.surface: Charley is throwing a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going ballistic' rearranges ITSCHARLEY, and the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going ballistic means losing control in a wild outburst, which is frenzied behaviour.

indicators.note: shredding the word carrot breaks it up so its letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool for shredding carrots, oddly described as surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: A trocar is a sharp-pointed surgical instrument used to drain fluid.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the drink surrounds the letter

parts.note: lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A makeshift fort with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: LAGER goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a defensive circle of wagons, a makeshift camp fortification.

clue.text: This can put over a part of the 17th century

parts.note: taken as written
a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: recast means the words or cast are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A playful string of words about casting.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its company of performers.

clue.text: "No man is an island …" — this includes Arabs

indicators.note: this, the quotation, includes the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Donne's famous line, said to contain some Arabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this includes' points to the letters running through 'No man is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omanis are people of Oman, an Arab nation.

definitions.meaning: want in the sense of a lack or shortcoming
to desert one side for another

explanation.surface: Wishing to switch sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a lack or flaw, and to defect is to desert to the other side.
